review_candidates.title: Bookkeeper (with Clio experience)
review_candidates.company: Move Your Business, Virtual Employment Agency
review_candidates.description: MOVE Your Business is proud to represent Geraci LLP, a nationally recognized law firm dedicated to serving private lenders across the United States. Geraci LLP provides legal services at every stage of the lending process—from drafting customized loan documentation to ensuring compliance with complex regulatory requirements and mitigating risk. With deep industry expertise, the firm advises clients on entity formation, licensing, litigation, documentation, and evolving regulatory challenges. Geraci LLP’s client-first approach is strategic, consistent, and tailored to meet the unique needs of every private lender. On behalf of Geraci LLP, we are seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Bookkeeper to join our growing team remotely. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced professional environment and has hands-on experience with legal accounting systems and U.S. bookkeeping practices. The Bookkeeper will be responsible for maintaining the firm's financial records, processing transactions, reconciling accounts, and supporting the overall accounting function. This individual will play a critical role in ensuring the accuracy and integrity of the firm's financial information while working closely with leadership and external accounting professionals. The successful candidate must have practical experience using Clio, QuickBooks, and Gusto, and possess a strong understanding of bookkeeping principles applicable to U.S. businesses. Note: Please submit your resume in English so we can effectively assess your qualifications. Benefits:  Competitive salary  Strong support system  Salary increase starting in your first year of employment (based on performance) Health benefit ($30/month)  Paid holiday leaves (depending on the holidays that the client observes)  Paid sick leaves (sick leave convertible to cash if perfect attendance)  Paid planned leaves  Internet Allowance ($25/month) Key Responsibilities General Bookkeeping Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial records. Record and classify daily financial transactions. Reconcile bank accounts, credit cards, and other balance sheet accounts. Review and monitor cash flow and account balances. Assist with month-end and year-end closing processes. Accounts Payable & Receivable Process vendor invoices and payments. Monitor accounts receivable and follow up on outstanding balances. Prepare client invoices and assist with collections as needed. Reconcile client payments received through various platforms. Legal Accounting Utilize Clio to maintain billing records and financial information. Coordinate with attorneyts and staff regarding billing matters. Ensure accuracy between Clio and QuickBooks records. Assist in maintaining compliance with legal accounting procedures and internal controls. Payroll Support Process and reconcile payroll through Gusto. Review payroll reports and ensure payroll expenses are accurately recorded. Coordinate employee reimbursements and payroll-related adjustments. Financial Reporting Prepare monthly bookkeeping reports and supporting schedules. Generate reports for management review. Assist external accountants with tax preparation and audit requests. Maintain organized electronic financial records and documentation. Qualifications and Requirements Minimum 3 years of bookkeeping experience using U.S. accounting practices at an American law firm. Demonstrated proficiency with: Clio QuickBooks Gusto Strong understanding of: Accounts payable and receivable Bank reconciliations General ledger maintenance Financial reporting Payroll accounting Exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills. Ability to handle confidential information with discretion. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities. Two professional references and a valid criminal background check issued within the last 60 days are required for all successful applicants. Completion of intake paperwork, including submission of a valid tax identification number (e.g., Social Security Number, Social Insurance Number, or the country’s equivalent), is required before onboarding. Preferred: Previous experience working in a law firm or other professional services environment. Experience with multi-state payroll and accounting. Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field. Familiarity with trust accounting principles and legal billing practices. Working Hours: Full Time (40 hours per week) Monday through Friday 8 a.m. - 5 p.m. Pacific Time Salary Range: $800 - $1,000 + $55 Allowance per month  About Us: MOVE Your Business is an outsourcing company based in Southern California, dedicated to empowering both businesses and professionals. We connect growing companies with skilled virtual talent while creating meaningful, long-term opportunities for our team members. As a fast-growing player in the outsourcing space, we’re committed to building partnerships that drive success and to fostering a supportive, inclusive environment where our people can thrive and grow with us.

review_candidates.title: Avionics Design Manager
review_candidates.description: The future of aerospace and defense starts here. Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands. The Avionics Manager is a key engineering leadership role responsible for leading an integrated team focused on FPGA design and verification, firmware/software development, and avionics test engineering in support of advanced aerospace and defense systems. The organization is responsible for developing FPGA-based digital designs, verification environments, embedded and test software, and automated electrical test solutions used to develop, qualify, and produce mission-critical avionics hardware. The team also develops and maintains component-level test equipment, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) capabilities, automated acceptance and qualification test systems, and provides technical oversight of subcontracted avionics development and test activities. As an Avionics Manager, you will lead a multidisciplinary team of FPGA Design Engineers, FPGA Verification Engineers, Firmware/Test Software Engineers, and Electrical Test Engineers responsible for delivering reliable, high-quality avionics solutions that meet demanding technical, schedule, and mission requirements. You will be responsible for technical execution, resource planning, staffing, process improvement, and cross-functional coordination across Engineering, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality, and Program Management. Responsibilities Lead an integrated engineering organization responsible for FPGA design, FPGA verification, firmware/software development, and avionics test engineering. Manage the development, integration, verification, qualification, and transition to production of avionics hardware and associated software throughout the product lifecycle. Ensure robust engineering processes, design reviews, verification plans, configuration management, and quality standards are consistently applied while maintaining the agility required to meet program schedules. Provide technical leadership and organizational direction for FPGA architecture, verification strategy, automated test development, and system integration activities. Manage team staffing, workload balancing, hiring, mentoring, and employee development across multiple engineering disciplines. Develop and maintain department resource plans aligned with program priorities and strategic business objectives. Own department schedule execution, technical performance, and milestone achievement across multiple programs. Monitor and communicate program health, technical risks, staffing needs, and execution status to Avionics Director. Identify technical, schedule, and cost risks and drive mitigation plans across engineering organizations. Foster collaboration between Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, and Program Management to improve product development and production readiness. Support proposal efforts, technology roadmaps, make/buy decisions, and strategic planning for avionics development capabilities. Provide technical oversight of subcontractors and suppliers supporting FPGA, firmware, and avionics test development. Required Qualifications Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical discipline. 10+ years of experience developing FPGA-based digital systems, embedded software, avionics electronics, or automated test systems. 3+ years of engineering leadership experience managing multidisciplinary engineering teams. Demonstrated experience leading complex hardware/software development efforts from concept through qualification and production. Strong understanding of FPGA development, digital design, verification methodologies, embedded software, and electrical test systems. Experience leading cross-functional engineering teams in a fast-paced development environment. Excellent communication, organizational, and leadership skills. Must be a U.S. Person with the ability to perform work subject to ITAR/EAR regulations and applicable program requirements. Preferred Experience Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related technical field. Experience developing avionics or mission electronics for aerospace or defense applications. Experience with FPGA development and verification methodologies, including SystemVerilog and UVM. Experience managing embedded software and automated test software development. Familiarity with Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL), qualification testing, and environmental testing of electronic hardware. Experience with configuration management, requirements traceability, and engineering lifecycle processes. Experience managing technical execution across multiple concurrent programs. Project or program management experience. Active or ability to obtain a U.S. Department of Defense Security Clearance. Colorado law requires us to tell you the base compensation range of this role, which is $160,000 - $200,000, determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy. Classification: Full-time Exempt Benefits Include: (Please note, Interns are not eligible for benefits) Unlimited PTO - Vacation, Sick, Personal, and Bereavement Paid Parental and Adoptive Leave Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance Tax Advantage Accounts (HSA/FSA) Employer Paid Short and Long Term Disability, Basic Life, AD&D Additional Benefit Options Including Voluntary Life and Emergency Medical Transport EAP Program Retirement Savings Plan - 401k with Company Match How To Apply Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by filling out the application below and clicking "Submit Application". This position will be posted for a minimum of 3 days and will remain open until filled or adjusted based on the volume of applicants. NOTE: Research suggests that women and BIPOC individuals may self-select out of opportunities if they don't meet 100% of the job requirements. We encourage anyone who believes they have the skills and the drive necessary to succeed here to apply for this role. Must be a U.S. Person (this includes U.S. Citizens and Permanent Residents). Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance. We’re an equal-opportunity employer. You will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status. No outside recruiters, please.

As a global engineering and construction company specializing in the semiconductor industry, UIS brings together talented people, technical expertise, and innovative solutions to deliver the most complex and critical projects in the industry. Our U.S. team is helping build the next generation of advanced semiconductor manufacturing facilities, working alongside some of the world's leading technology companies. Our work requires precision, collaboration, accountability, and a commitment to doing things the right way—from the planning and engineering stages through construction and project completion. As UIS continues to grow, we are building more than projects. We are building teams, developing careers, and creating opportunities for talented professionals to make a meaningful impact. If you are looking for an opportunity to work on challenging projects, grow your career, and be part of something bigger, we invite you to build the future with UIS. WHAT WE OFFER Comprehensive Benefits – Medical, Dental, Vision, Short-Term Disability (STD), Long-Term Disability (LTD), and Life Insurance provided at no cost to employees. Competitive Compensation – Competitive salaries and opportunities for performance-based incentives. Career Growth – Opportunities to develop your skills, take on new challenges, and grow with a rapidly expanding organization, supported by education reimbursement for eligible employees pursuing continued learning and professional development. Meaningful Work – The opportunity to contribute to some of the most advanced semiconductor construction projects in the country. Collaborative Environment – Work alongside experienced professionals across engineering, construction, project management, safety, procurement, and operations. Summary: We are seeking a highly motivated Associate Engineer - FMCS - to join our team and contribute to the design, implementation, and execution of advanced control systems in a construction environment. This position offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in field engineering, automation, and construction while working alongside experienced industry professionals. You will assist in the process of assembly, troubleshoot, and repair of the Facility Management & Control System. Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned. Perform requirements classification of clients, communicating project requirements and design review with internal & external design team. Understand drawing and review specifications and estimation. Conduct onsite inspection to ensure that workmanship conforms with specifications and assure adherence to construction schedules. Assist with onsite inspections, system evaluations, and compliance checks. Anticipate and prevent problems from rising. Planning of MEP & C/R & AAS I&C Construction drawing Contribute to the installation, calibration, and maintenance of instrumentation and control elements. Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to optimize control system performance. Maintain accurate documentation and assist in developing technical reports. Provide daily, weekly, and monthly reports for internal use and client communication. Participate in material tracking and procurement coordination to ensure seamless project execution. Adhere to safety regulations while working in a construction site environment. Assist procurement team on the procurement of FMCS systems equipment & materials’ and assist in contractors’ awards. Review & reply RFI (Request for Information) and change orders. Review progress reports, materials used and costs, contract payment application, and adjust work schedules as indicated by the reports. Other responsibilities as assigned. Qualifications: The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. 0+ years of related work experience, in Control systems planning preferred. Skills and Competencies: Strong theoretical foundation in control systems, automation, and industrial instrumentation. Planning of MEP & C/R & AAS I&C Construction drawing Good understanding of FMCS systems including hardware and operational documentation of instruments & control elements, PLC, DCS and control networking. Familiarity with Sensors, analyzers, actuators, HMI to measure and control variables like pressure, temperature, flow, level, humidity, pH, force, and speed. Understand isometrics, P&ID (Piping and Instrumentation Design) and CAD layout drawings specifically for FMCS systems. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite products (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, Teams). Ability to use engineering software, such as AutoCAD, or others. Excellent organizational and time management skills. High problem-solving skills. High level of attention to detail, and highly organized. Ability to effectively prioritize responsibilities depending on project needs. Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers and employees. Ability to develop and maintain successful relationships with all levels of employees, clients, and subcontractors. Must be able to work under pressure and meet deadlines while maintaining a professional attitude. Ability to work in a construction site environment (trailer office). Language Proficiency: Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English. Ability to communicate in Mandarin, preferred. Nice to have: Internship or research experience in control systems, industrial automation, or instrumentation. Verbal communication skills in Mandarin. Additional Requirements: Must have and maintain a valid driver’s license. May be required to travel to other sites within Arizona to perform certain work functions. Physical Demands: The physical demands described here are representative of those that a candidate must meet to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Frequently stand and walk for extended periods throughout the workday. Frequently lift, carry, push, and pull materials weighing up to 50 pounds, and occasionally lift heavier items with assistance or mechanical equipment. Bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, and reach to perform assigned tasks. Use hands and fingers to handle, feel, grasp, and operate tools, equipment, or materials. Perform repetitive motions involving the hands, wrists, and arms. Climb ladders, stairs, or elevated surfaces as required by the job. Maintain visual acuity sufficient to read labels, instructions, safety signage, and documentation. Maintain balance and coordination while moving materials or operating equipment. Ability to work in physically demanding environments requiring frequent movement and manual labor. Work Environment: Exposure to dust, noise, vibration, and moving mechanical equipment. Indoor and/or outdoor work environments, which may include varying temperatures and weather conditions. Work in confined spaces, elevated areas, or active job sites, depending on project requirements. Required use of personal protective equipment (PPE) such as hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, steel-toe boots, and high-visibility vests. Interaction with powered industrial equipment, tools, and vehicles. Equal Employment Opportunity: UIS is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
